books.title: CODIT Separatrix Manifold Model
books.subtitle: Wall 4 as a Chaotic Separatrix in Tree Wound Compartmentalization
books.desc: Reframes the CODIT model as a phase-separatrix manifold. Wall 4 — the barrier zone generated by the cambium after wounding — is a chaotic separatrix: a 2D manifold that determines whether a wounded system decays or integrates. Trees do not block off injury; they redefine their ontological boundary around it.

books.title: Xeric Semiotic Shield Theory
books.subtitle: Semiotic Defense Mechanisms in Xeric Plant Morphogenesis
books.desc: Proposes that plants in high-stress environments engage in active semiotic processing — decoding environmental signals and responding with morphological configurations that constitute adaptive geometry. Secondary metabolites are reframed as symbolic infrastructure, not defensive byproducts. The leaf is a glyph. Form follows interpretation.

books.title: Solar Arbor Topology
books.subtitle: Magnetic Trees as Consciousness Template — A Mythogenic Synthesis Across Scales
books.desc: Documents the isomorphism between solar magnetic trees (stellar scale), terrestrial biological trees (planetary scale), and consciousness structure trees (cognitive scale). The pattern repeats because topology is substrate-independent. The geometry is the same all the way down.

books.title: Geometry of Neural Space
books.subtitle: Non-Orientable Manifolds, Hyperbolic Expansion, and the Topology of Learning
books.desc: The neural manifold underlying consciousness is non-orientable — no stable inside/outside, no consistent handedness. Learning is topological reconfiguration of phase space; memory is a stable basin topology; trauma is a failed compartmentalization. The brain solves the same optimization problem as the tree: infinite connectivity within finite volume, via hyperbolic geometry.

books.title: Semiospheric Anisotropy and the Treefall Axiom
books.subtitle: Mythogenic Phase Transition, Gödelian Supercession, and the Arrow of Semantic Time
books.desc: A Treefall event — any irreversible instantiation moment — creates a Gödelian supercession: a phase bifurcation whose semantic weight exceeds its origin frame. Semantics is isotropic until symbolic activation; then it becomes anisotropic, creating an arrow of meaning analogous to the thermodynamic arrow of time. Introduces the Semantical Hyperbola as an alternative to the point singularity.

books.title: Dark Matter as Information Knots
books.subtitle: Causal Recursion, Gravitational Lensing, and the Universe as Archive
books.desc: Dark matter reframed not as invisible mass but as a network of self-referential causal loops — information knots woven into spacetime. The universe is mythogenic and self-archiving: ~85% of its gravitational content is composed of causal memory. Includes testable predictions for lensing asymmetry via modified Poisson equation.
